arch_opening: There is an update available — version 1.3.0. Before we get into today's work, I want to walk through what changed. One of the changes introduces manifest.md, which gives me a clear picture of your specific setup before I walk you through anything. I will look at your actual files and tell you exactly what applies to you. This should take a few minutes.

changes.title: manifest.md introduced
changes.what_changed: new-setup.md now generates manifest.md at the end of first-time setup. manifest.md is the single source of truth for this install — team names, role filenames, handoff directory, repo, and installed version.
changes.old_behavior: No record of how the install was configured. Version check had to guess at filenames.
changes.new_behavior: Arch generates manifest.md during setup. Version check reads it to understand the exact setup before walking through any change.
changes.user_impact_plain: New installs get manifest.md automatically. If you are an existing user, I will create it with you now — it takes two minutes and unlocks accurate version checks going forward.
changes.how_to_assess:
Check if manifest.md exists in the project root. If it does not exist: (1) Ask the user to confirm their current role filenames — what is the architect role file called? builder? reviewer? What is their handoff directory? Do they have a project repo URL? (2) Show them this example and fill it in together:

# Three Man Team — Manifest

version: v1.3.0
installed: 2026-06-05

## Team
architect: Arch — ARCHITECT.md
builder: Bob — BUILDER.md
reviewer: Richard — REVIEWER.md

## Project
handoff_dir: handoff/
repo: https://github.com/yourname/yourrepo
branch: main
context_file: CLAUDE.md

(3) Create manifest.md in their project root with the confirmed values. If manifest.md already exists, read it and confirm the values look correct — offer to update any that are wrong.
changes.user_decision: I need to create manifest.md for your install. It will take about two minutes. Ready?

changes.title: Version check upgraded — registry model with critical checkpoints
changes.what_changed: Version check now reads a version registry from releases/latest.json instead of a single version pointer. Critical updates are mandatory checkpoints; non-critical are optional. Fallback to VERSION file if manifest.md is missing.
changes.old_behavior: Fetched GitHub releases API for latest tag. Walked migration_steps linearly.
changes.new_behavior: Fetches raw releases/latest.json. Parses versions[] array. Processes critical checkpoints in order before optional updates.
changes.user_impact_plain: Version checks are now smarter — mandatory upgrades are flagged and handled first, optional ones are your choice.
changes.how_to_assess: Read the user Architect role file Session Start step 2. Does it reference versions[] and critical checkpoints? If it still hits api.github.com or reads a single version field, the upgrade applies.
changes.user_decision: Your version check uses the old method. Want me to update it? One edit to your Architect role file.

changes.title: VERSION file retired
changes.what_changed: VERSION file in the project root is no longer the primary version source. Version is tracked in manifest.md. VERSION is read as fallback only if manifest.md is missing.
changes.old_behavior: VERSION file was the sole version source for the version check.
changes.new_behavior: manifest.md is the primary source. VERSION file is fallback only.
changes.user_impact_plain: If you have a VERSION file, you can remove it once manifest.md is in place. Nothing breaks if you leave it.
changes.how_to_assess: Check if a VERSION file exists in the project root and if manifest.md also exists.
changes.user_decision: You have both VERSION and manifest.md. Want me to remove VERSION? It is no longer needed.
